title: Introduce gpu_nodepool_fence TF module and iam_scoped_subnet_resolver for tenant-scoped state mapping
author: Asha Raman
description: Motivation: Private installs need stronger tenant isolation for GPU node pools, predictable network allocation, and a safer tfstate migration path when moving from a single cluster tfstate to tenant-scoped state shards. This PR introduces two Terraform modules and a lightweight state-mapping helper: 1) gpu_nodepool_fence: opinionated GPU nodepool module that emits node pool resources with tenant-scoped IAM bindings, explicit taint/toleration templates, kubelet flags for node fencing, and optional preflight driver hooks. 2) iam_scoped_subnet_resolver: subnet allocator that resolves non-overlapping /24+/26 CIDR slices per tenant via claims and emits subnet attachment records and cross-account route table associations. 3) tfstate_mapper helper (input-only minimal module): generates a mapping file and migration plan to atomically split cluster-level TF state into tenant-sharded state buckets and produces an advisory plan for state move operations. Key design goals: tenant isolation (IAM least privilege), deterministic subnet assignment to avoid AZ-affinity drift, safe rollback surface (tfstate_mapper produces reversible plan), and minimal disruption to existing nodepool naming. Backwards compatibility: existing installs remain unchanged until operator applies the tfstate_mapper plan; the new modules are opt-in. This PR contains a migration README, example usage, unit tests for CIDR calculation, and e2e validation scripts that run terraform plan against a mock backend. See commits for details.

c8d5a77: add tfstate_mapper helper and migration README with stepwise instructions
d12f9e3: tests: add unit tests for cidr allocation and name collision detection

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can we guarantee that the deterministic CIDR allocator will not produce collisions across parallel runs? Please add a collision-resilient check and retry policy.

Asha Raman: Added a simple reservation lease and a fast-forward check. The allocator now computes a hashed offset from tenant-id and probes for existing allocations before committing. Included unit tests that simulate parallel claims.
Marta Silva: Concerned about the tfstate migration being disruptive. We need a step-by-step plan and a reversible path if a move partially fails.

Asha Raman: Added tfstate_mapper README with a three-phase plan: dry-run (plan-only), staged copy to tenant bucket with state lock detection, and final state move with verified drift checks. Also included rollback commands and verification scripts.
Diego Alvarez: IAM roles look fine but we should scope the instance-profile role to a narrower permission set for node registration and kubelet bootstrap only.
Asha Raman: Tightened the IAM policy, removed broad ec2:Describe* calls, and documented required extra privileges for optional driver hooks.
Marta Silva: Please add an explicit opt-in flag in the private-installer chart values to switch to tenant-scoped subnets and nodepool fencing.
Asha Raman: Added values.yaml entry and updated the example in charts/private/values.yaml. Default remains disabled to avoid accidental flips during upgrades.
release_notes: Introduces gpu_nodepool_fence and iam_scoped_subnet_resolver Terraform modules and a tfstate_mapper helper for tenant-sharded state. Opt-in migration path documented. Security: tighter IAM for node bootstrap. Note: Requires operator-driven migration; no automatic state moves.
